channel.title: Eastern Daily Press - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Eastern Daily Press (edp24.co.uk)

item.title: City airport objects to plans for hundreds homes over solar panel glare fears
item.description: Officers for Norwich Airport have once again raised concerns over the development of hundreds of homes in Thorpe Marriott.

item.title: City Hall under fire over multi-million-pound regeneration of 14th century venue
item.description: Norwich City Council has been told to count the costs of delays to reopening the Halls, which is about to reopen a year later than planned.

item.title: Cafe and visitor centre being built at country park progresses
item.description: Construction of a new cafe and visitor centre at a park on the outskirts of Norwich has progressed. The project will ensure the site is more accessible.

item.title: Thousands caught by bus lane cameras as Norfolk council nets record £1.2m in fines
item.description: A record £1.2m has been paid into County Hall's coffers by motorists fined for driving into Norfolk's bus lanes - sparking claims cameras are being used as 'cash cows'.

item.title: Ongoing police investigation into death of Gorleston man
item.description: An inquest into the death of a 39-year-old man from Gorleston has been adjourned for a further three months due to an ongoing police investigation.

item.title: Fresh plans revealed for four new homes on village farmland
item.description: A developer has launched a fresh bid to build four new homes on village farmland.

item.title: Open for business! Five new cafes for people to enjoy a sweet treat
item.description: Chapel Yard in Mattishall and the Nest Cafe in Burnham Deepdale are among some of the new cafes that have opened recently in Norfolk.

item.title: Owner of listed cottage could be forced to remove plastic windows
item.description: The owner of a listed building in Holt, north Norfolk, could be forced to remove double-glazed windows after installing them without permission.

item.title: Tanning salon gets green light for illuminated signs
item.description: Planners for Norwich City Council have allowed Clubtan to install illuminated signs on its Prince of Wales shop front.

item.title: Make the most of early mornings - and it will make you feel so much better
item.description: If you’re a regular reader of this column, you’ll know I have a passion for positive ageing which I like to pass on to you.
